featured_videos.commentary: The social friction Andrew's laying out here is *exactly* what our 45-plus audience deals with constantly, and I love that the top comments are basically a masterclass in boundary-setting. What's striking is how many people mention just stopping the conversation short, "I feel better eating this way," and moving on. That's not avoidance, it's wisdom. You don't owe anyone a ted talk about your food choices, especially when the other person's already decided you're wrong. The real win in these comments isn't the arguments people won. it's the ones they stopped having.

featured_videos.creator: The Daily Ribeye
featured_videos.editorial_title: 3 Carnivore Meals That Helped Us Lose 40 Pounds
featured_videos.commentary: What's hitting me about this video is how real the community response is. People aren't just applauding the weight loss (though that 40 pounds is solid), they're noticing something deeper. the energy shift, the consistency, the willingness to show actual meals instead of hype. That comment about butter being the missing piece? That's exactly what I see in coaching conversations. People think carnivore is about restriction, but it's really about satisfaction, and fat is what keeps you full and stops the cravings cycle. The budget-conscious flat iron steak mention matters too, because this diet doesn't need to be expensive to work. What makes this resonate is they're not selling perfection. they're just documenting what actually stuck for them, and that's the kind of honest content that moves people from curiosity to action.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore Diet Linked to HEART ATTACKS?
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore Diet Linked to HEART ATTACKS?
featured_videos.commentary: The comments section here is the real story. You've got people saying they reversed heart disease on carnivore, got zero CAC scores, resolved inflammation completely. Then you've got the flip side: the "80% carnivore" crowd who are probably still eating their kids' leftover pizza and wondering why they're not seeing results. The gap between strict adherence and casual label-wearing matters enormously when we're talking about heart health. What Dr. Hampton nails here is that one bad study or one elevated cholesterol number doesn't prove the diet kills you, just like one good number doesn't prove it saves you. You need the full picture: CAC scores, inflammation markers, actual artery imaging, not just LDL panic. The real takeaway for your health is stop letting one doctor's outdated playbook (statins for everyone) dictate your entire metabolic future.

featured_videos.title: What to Eat When Sugar Cravings Hit on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Jenny Mitich
featured_videos.editorial_title: What to Eat When Sugar Cravings Hit on Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here reveal something I see constantly in coaching: cravings aren't actually about willpower, they're about satiety. Notice how the people who cracked it point to the same thing. fat. Butter on eggs, tallow, clarified butter on pork rinds. One commenter nailed it: "sugar cravings usually mean I haven't eaten enough fat." That's not an accident. The ones struggling are often the same people eating lean meat and skipping the fattier cuts. If you're still battling sweet cravings after a few weeks on carnivore, your macro balance is probably off. Check out our guide on macros for carnivore to see if you're actually hitting your fat targets. What also stands out is how many people mention sleep as a trigger. that person who said they crave carbs without good sleep isn't alone. Tired nervous systems reach for quick energy, and salt and electrolytes can genuinely help stabilize that impulse before it becomes a craving.
